summary.title: A Distributed Systems Reading List
summary.one_liner: A curated, annotated list of papers and articles on distributed systems design, covering mindset shifts, CAP and consistency tradeoffs, large-scale Google and Amazon systems, consensus (Paxos, Raft), and gossip and peer-to-peer protocols.
takeaways: Distributed systems require a change in how you think about design; big servers, databases and transactions do not solve everything.
CAP and related results frame the consistency versus availability tradeoff, and two-phase commit is not always the right tool.
Reading Paxos Made Simple before and after the other consensus papers is recommended; Raft is offered as an alternative to Paxos.
The list points to landmark systems papers from Google (MapReduce, GFS, BigTable, Spanner) and peer-to-peer and gossip protocol papers (Chord, Kademlia, Pastry, SWIM).
summary.summary: This is a reading list rather than a tutorial, grouped into sections: mindset and design essays, Amazon's service-oriented culture, large-scale systems papers from Google, consistency and CAP tradeoffs, foundational theory papers, consensus algorithms, and gossip and peer-to-peer protocols. Each entry is a one-line annotation with a link-style title, often by authors such as Pat Helland, Werner Vogels, Jim Gray and Leslie Lamport. Some entries are noted as paywalled. The page itself contains no original technical explanations, so it works mainly as a pointer to further material.
